newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends firmer, but well off session highs.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends firmer, but well off session highs.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended moderately higher Monday, but toward the bottom of the day's range, as local long liquidation pared early gains, dealers said.

The benchmark December contract finished up $8 a tonne, at $1,376, after ranging from $1,387 to $1,375. Second-month March settled $9 higher at $1,409, while the remaining months closed $8 to $15 firmer.
Floor sources said commission house and speculative buying boosted values from the outset, touching off buy-stops in the most-active December contract in the upper $1,370s to low $1,380s.
But the December position stopped short of key resistance at $1,390, a double top on the charts, and traders said the buying subsided.
Although December faltered near the $1,390 mark, traders expect the nearby contract to test its next upside objective at $1,405-$1,408, a chart gap formed late last month.
The latest U.S. CFTC Commitment of Traders report, which showed an increase in speculative or non-commercial short positions, also buoyed cocoa prices today, traders said.
"I think if the market can get above $1,390 (in the December contract) it will entice short specs to start short covering," one trader said.
Another dealer said the lingering effect of UK commodity traders ED&F Man's report may have encouraged buyers.

Man said in its September report released Thursday that grindings in the five largest processing nations rose over 12 percent in the second quarter of 1996, and estimated that grindings will increase by six percent this season, the highest growth rate since 1988/89.
Volume was light, at an estimated 4,767 lots.
